What the reviewers asked for

Three ESWA reviewers (and our own audit, R0) asked us to: fix bugs and test-set leakage that invalidate the submitted numbers; compare against strong and simple baselines under one protocol; give seed-level results with confidence intervals and non-parametric tests; justify design choices (BatchNorm, window length, dropout, smoothing, sensor order) with proper ablations; explain the FD004 Score; and soften superiority claims.

What we did: the paper's story in four steps

  1. Corrected original model θ*. We fixed the two attention bugs (R0.1, R0.2), the leakage and test-selection problems, and re-tuned the submitted two-branch model on validation only (exp_B6). Under this protocol, all three reproduced Transformer baselines (PatchTST, iTransformer, Crossformer) had lower mean test RMSE than θ* on all four subsets (combined_table_v4.md).
  2. Diagnosis. Code-level analysis found six likely causes (A–F, section 3.4), for example that 80–88% of the channel-encoder query rows output only the mean of the values, and that the fusion gives the temporal branch 1.5–9.6% weight. None was isolated by its own ablation; the wording is "consistent with", never "shows".
  3. D1 → D4 validation screen. Four designs, each addressing more causes, were screened on validation under a frozen preregistration (exp_B15). D4 had the lowest screening score and was the only design taken to test. The screen is a validation screen, not a factorial test (paper_plan D14 L6).
  4. D4 as the result. The frozen D4 (exp_B16) was then probed by round-4/5 sensitivity arms and compared with two new simple baselines (LSTM, ridge).

What we found (verified)

  • Preregistered primary (D4 − validation-chosen best baseline Bk, 20 seed pairs): Inconclusive. Mean Δ -0.20 test RMSE, D4 lower in 15/20 pairs, exact two-sided Wilcoxon p = 0.0696. Secondary: non-inferior at a 0.5-cycle margin (one-sided p = 0.00043).
  • D4 vs θ*: pooled Δ −1.25 RMSE (p 0.0004, 16/20). Per-subset cells: see the next bullet.
  • Per-subset comparisons (secondary, not the preregistered primary; the primary above is Inconclusive, p 0.0696). A per-subset difference is called significant only if Holm p < 0.05 and the engine-bootstrap CI excludes 0, and only if the hierarchical CI also excludes 0 (paper_plan D22, D51). These cells meet the rule: D4 − θ* on FD002 and FD003, D4 − iTransformer on FD002, D4 − LSTM on FD003, and D4 − ridge on FD001–FD004. For ridge on FD001, the hierarchical CI lies within Monte Carlo error of 0. D4 − PatchTST on FD002 meets both numerical conditions, but its hierarchical CI [−1.31, +0.03] includes 0, so it is not called significant. No subset meets the rule against the best baseline or against Crossformer. These are cell-level statements; they do not support “D4 significantly outperforms the baselines”.
  • No significance claim vs PatchTST, pooled or per subset (pooled p 0.0484 uncorrected; Holm-5 0.145, a family that was not preregistered; D12, D51).
  • Rankings by mean test RMSE (D48): FD001 D4 is 4th of 7 (Crossformer 12.97 lowest); FD002 D4 lowest (12.17); FD003 D4 lowest (11.55), PatchTST 11.60, no difference shown; FD004 D4 is 3rd (LSTM 13.36 < Crossformer 13.53 < D4 13.80). D4 is not ranked above the LSTM on FD004 (D34).
  • Simple baselines. D4 is lower than the LSTM pooled (Δ −1.24, p 0.0037, 16/20) and than ridge on every pair (20/20). The LSTM row is a conservative estimate: 16 of its 48 tuning trials did not converge within 150 epochs (D34).
  • Smoothing. Without the causal EMA, D4's test RMSE rises by +2.95 pooled, but the excess error sits in end-padded short test engines. On unpadded windows no effect of smoothing on test RMSE was shown (pooled +0.14, p 0.60). A validation-only simulation reproduces the pattern (D47).
  • Other sensitivity checks (all on the frozen D4, nothing re-selected): RMSE rises as the training-engine fraction falls (Page's L p ≤ 0.011 on every subset); LayerNorm vs BatchNorm shows no RMSE difference (LN Score worse, secondary); on validation no tested window length (30, 40) beat L = 50 and no tied dropout value was Holm-significantly different. None of these supports the word "optimal".
  • Reproducibility. Strict deterministic mode for every round-4/5 run; 20/20 seed-0 cells of the five main models and four reviewer re-runs reproduced bit for bit on the same machine (D36, D41).

3.1 ProbSparse multi-head attention as implemented (Informer; attn.py, unchanged since round 1)

Per sequence and head, with n tokens and sampling factor c = 5:

$$U = \min\big(c\lceil \ln n\rceil,\ n\big), \qquad u = \min\big(c\lceil \ln n\rceil,\ n\big)$$ $$\bar M(q_i) = \max_{j \in S_i} \frac{q_i k_j^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{j \in S_i} \frac{q_i k_j^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}}, \qquad |S_i| = U \text{ sampled keys}$$ $$\mathcal T = \operatorname{top\text{-}u}_i\, \bar M(q_i), \qquad z_i = \begin{cases} \sum_{j=1}^{n} \operatorname{softmax}_j\!\left(\frac{q_i k_j^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) v_j, & i \in \mathcal T \\[4pt] \frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n} v_j, & i \notin \mathcal T \end{cases}$$ $$\operatorname{MHA}(Z) = [Z^{(1)}, \dots, Z^{(H)}]\,W_O + b_O, \qquad Q = ZW_Q + b_Q,\ K = ZW_K + b_K,\ V = ZW_V + b_V$$

Keys are sampled at random during training and with a fixed generator (eval seed 0) at evaluation (RULES §13). If u ≥ n, every query is kept and the layer is exact softmax attention. The encoder layer around it (TBN): $Z_1 = \mathrm{BN}(Z + \mathrm{Drop}(\mathrm{MHA}(Z)))$, $Z_2 = \mathrm{BN}(Z_1 + \mathrm{Drop}(\mathrm{FFN}(Z_1)))$, FFN = Linear(d, dff) → GELU → Linear(dff, d). Source: workspace/experiments/round_01/exp_A1/ARCHITECTURE.md (workspace, not in release). The manuscript prints a different score, $S(q_i) = \lVert q_i\rVert_2/\sqrt{d_k}$ with $u = c\log L$. That mismatch is R1.32 (Deferred-Writing, Simon).

3.4 Diagnosis: why θ* trails the baselines (causes A–F)

Source: workspace/research/round_03.md (workspace, not in release) §2. Each cause has code-level or artifact evidence. None was isolated by a dedicated ablation. The D1 → D4 chain is one validation study per design on three subsets, with 12 non-independent pairs. Its deltas are descriptive. Allowed wording: "consistent with", never "shows that cause X explains" (workspace/research/round_04.md (workspace, not in release) §2.3). Tuning budget alone does not explain the gap: θ0, which was tuned on test, also loses to Crossformer on every subset (workspace/verdicts/round_02.md (workspace, not in release)).

CauseIn plain wordsEvidence (numbers and artifact)First design that addresses it
A. Channel branch is mostly "mean of V" plus sampling noiseMost channel tokens never look at other tokens. They all output the same average vector. Which tokens do attend depends on random key samples.80–88% lazy rows at θ* (table 3.2). On the round-1 FD001 model, exact attention at evaluation gives RMSE 56.4, so the trained network relies on the lazy rows (workspace/experiments/round_01/exp_A1/README.md (workspace, not in release)).D1
B. Channel tokens drown the temporal branchThe fusion averages all tokens equally: 150–240 channel tokens against 3–16 temporal tokens.Temporal share of the pooled vector 0.016 / 0.015 / 0.020 / 0.096 (workspace/experiments/round_03/exp_A9/shapes.md (workspace, not in release)).D2
C. Patching drops the newest cycles and some sensorsPatches are cut without padding, so the cycles closest to failure are never seen.θ* drops the newest 5 cycles on FD002/FD003 and 1 on FD001. The FD002 channel branch covers 14 of 16 sensors and never sees sm_20 or sm_21 in the original order (paper_plan D20; workspace/experiments/round_03/exp_A9/covered.md (workspace, not in release)).D2 (sensors), D3 (cycles)
D. Temporal branch removes level and sensor identityInstanceNorm removes each sensor's level, but the level carries the wear signal. The sensors are then averaged.Code: PatchTSTEncoder.forward. Supporting only: validation tuning of PatchTST chose revin: false on all 4 subsets (confounded random search).D3
E. Mean-pooling readoutThe head sees one averaged vector, so it cannot tell which sensor said what.workspace/experiments/round_02/exp_A4/ARCHITECTURE.md (workspace, not in release) §1–3 (all three baselines flatten per sensor).D3
F. Higher seed variance and costθ* results scatter more across seeds, and each trial costs more GPU time.Test std θ* 0.76 / 1.05 / 0.47 / 0.57 vs PatchTST 0.27 / 0.12 / 0.13 / 0.06 (combined_table v2.1). Cost per completed trial θ* 0.171 GPU-h vs 0.034–0.076 for the baselines (research/round_03.md §2.6).measured, not a design

Math. Per sensor i, with shared weights:

$$\mu_i = \tfrac1L\textstyle\sum_t x_{i,t},\quad \sigma_i = \big(\tfrac1L\sum_t (x_{i,t}-\mu_i)^2 + 10^{-6}\big)^{1/2},\quad \tilde x_i = (x_i - \mu_i)/\sigma_i$$ $$\hat x_i = [\tilde x_i;\ \tilde x_{i,L}\mathbf 1],\qquad p_{i,n}^0 = W_P\,\hat x_i[nS_t : nS_t + P_t] + b_P + \mathrm{PE}_n$$ $$a_i^0 = W_{in}x_i + b_{in} + e_{\mathrm{id}(i)} + W_s[\mu_i, \log\sigma_i]^\top$$

For layer ℓ = 1..K:

$$[a_i';\ p_i^{\ell}] = \mathrm{TBN}_t^{\ell}\big([a_i^{\ell-1};\ p_i^{\ell-1}]\big),\qquad [a_1^{\ell},\dots,a_C^{\ell}] = \mathrm{TBN}_c^{\ell}\big([a_1',\dots,a_C']\big)$$ $$\hat y = w_2^\top\mathrm{Drop}\big(\mathrm{GELU}(W_1\operatorname{vec}(a^K_{\pi_c(1)},\dots,a^K_{\pi_c(C)}) + b_1)\big) + b_2$$

πc sorts sensors by original id. Attention in both stages is exact (PyTorch SDPA), so no evaluation seed applies.

Patch count (R1.3, submitted Eq. 10). From final/src/saca_rul/shapes.py and embeddings.py (n_patches, n_patches_padded). Without padding, as in θ*'s code (unfold): $N = \lfloor (L-P)/S \rfloor + 1$, so the newest $(L-P) \bmod S$ cycles are dropped. D4 appends S copies of the last value and uses $N' = \lfloor (L-P)/S \rfloor + 2$. At the frozen exp_B16 configuration (L = 50): FD001 P = S = 15, N = 3, N' = 4; FD002–FD004 P = S = 20, N = 2, N' = 3. The time stage of each sensor therefore sees N' + 1 = 5 (FD001) or 4 (FD002–FD004) tokens, the anchor plus the patches; the sensor stage sees C anchors. Figure 2b shows the padding. The concerns.md R1.3 reviewer note records that the form of submitted Eq. 10 holds for D4's end padding; the floor and the manuscript wording are Simon's text (R1.3 stays Planned).

Search spaces differ per model, so these are not per-step timings.

Order invariance (R2.16, R1.39). Every D4 operation is a per-sensor map with shared weights, an identity embedding bound to the sensor, attention over sensors without positional encoding, BN over sensors, or a flatten in canonical id order. Hence $f_{D4}(\pi x) = f_{D4}(x)$ for every row permutation π in real arithmetic. Test T4 (float64): outputs equal to ≤ 3.3e-16. Retraining with permuted orders (exp_B18, post-result exploratory, validation only): pooled Δ +0.026 (p 0.294), at most 19% of the seed std; this measures only float-order and dropout effects (D16).

Intuition. Each sensor has one "spokesperson" token. It reads its own sensor's history, talks to the other sensors' spokespersons, and carries what it heard back to its own history at the next layer. Risks. Gains could come from the design's own selection rather than the architecture (D4 vs θ* is "design plus its own selection"); D4's total search is larger than any other row's (one of 4 designs). How it could be proven wrong. The preregistered primary would have to show D4 worse than Bk; it did not, but it also did not show D4 better (Inconclusive). Novelty.

D4’s two-stage, time-then-sensor attention over per-sensor patch tokens follows Crossformer (Zhang & Yan, 2023, Sec. 3.2) and, for C-MAPSS RUL, STAR (Fan et al., 2024); per-sensor temporal attention with weights shared across sensors, followed by a stage over the combined signal, was used for C-MAPSS RUL by STAT (Chadha et al., 2022). What D4 changes is that the cross-sensor stage runs only over one anchor token per sensor. The anchor also takes part in that sensor’s within-sensor attention. It carries the level of the input window before instance normalisation, a sensor-identity embedding, and the window mean and log standard deviation (statistics re-injection as in RevIN (Kim et al., 2022), Non-stationary Transformers (Liu et al., 2022) and DFormer (Liu et al., 2024a)). Closest priors for the anchor: Crossformer’s router vectors, MBT bottleneck tokens (Nagrani et al., 2021), TimeXer (Wang et al., 2024) and ChannelTokenFormer (Jang et al., 2026); whole-window sensor tokens with attention among them follow iTransformer (Liu et al., 2024b) and, for C-MAPSS RUL, Sun et al. (2025; with Fourier-transform tokens, memory tokens and RevIN) and He et al. (2025). No prior work found in these searches: workspace/research/round_05_lit_star.md (workspace, not in release) §6. Sun et al. (2025) was read in full on 2026-10-29: it has no patch tokens and no per-sensor token inside a within-sensor attention, so the distinct element holds (workspace/research/round_05_sun2025_read.md (workspace, not in release) §4; review/post_release_star/sun2025_verify.md §3). Further related work identified but not read in full is listed in §6.1.

Source: research/round_05_lit_star.md §5.2 (sha256 ab469f16…5b), accepted in review/post_release_star/verify.md Addenda C (C.4) and D (item 6); citations attached to RevIN, Non-stationary Transformers, MBT, TimeXer and ChannelTokenFormer per Addendum D (correction 2). “§6.1” refers to the same research note. Wording limits: no “first”, “novel”, “new mechanism” or “state-of-the-art”; no accuracy or cost comparison with STAR; exact attention and the removal of ProbSparse are not differentiators (they correct the submitted model; R1.21). The letter paragraph for R1.15 is in docs/response_letter_draft_v01.md §5.

4.4 New baselines under the same protocol (R1.19)

LSTM (exp_V2). Input (B, C, L) → transpose → unidirectional nn.LSTM(C, hidden, layers) → last time step → Dropout → Linear(hidden, 1). $h_t^{(\ell)} = \mathrm{LSTM}^{(\ell)}(h_t^{(\ell-1)}, h_{t-1}^{(\ell)})$, $\hat y = w^\top\mathrm{Drop}(h_L^{(\mathrm{top})}) + b$. Same 12-trial rule and shared draws (L, lr log-U[1e-5, 1e-3], weight decay, batch {64, 128, 256}), plus hidden {32, 64, 128}, layers {1, 2, 3}, dropout U[0, 0.30].

Ridge (exp_V3, CPU, float64). $\hat w, \hat b = \arg\min_{w,b} \sum_n (y_n - w^\top\mathrm{vec}(x_n) - b)^2 + \alpha\lVert w\rVert_2^2$ on the same TR-fitted, EMA-smoothed windows; 12-trial rule over L {30, 40, 50}, α log-U[1e-3, 1e3]. Selected: FD001 L 40, α 224.20; FD002–FD004 L 50, α 1.4957 (workspace/experiments/round_04/exp_V3/README.md (workspace, not in release)).

Score definition: published misprints and the never-cite list (paper_plan D52, D55; RULES §26, §28, §29). Step 8 above is the Score used for every reported result. The response letter carries this footnote (letter §3.3; research/round_05_lit_star.md §13, verbatim, accepted in verify.md Addenda C.5 and D, plus the Sun et al. (2025) sentence, review/post_release_star/sun2025_verify.md §4, C8):
Several published sources print the Score formula with an error, so we do not cite any of them for its form. Saxena et al. (2008, Eq. 11, p. 7) print a₁ = 10 and a₂ = 13, which contradicts their own statement on the same page and their Fig. 9 (p. 8) that late predictions are penalised more heavily. DFormer (Liu et al., 2024a, Eq. 25, p. 7) prints a minus sign in both exponents, including the late case. STAR (Fan et al., 2024, Eq. 9, p. 13) prints the early case as exp(−(y − ŷ)/13) − 1, which contradicts its own text. Li et al. (2025, Eq. 14, p. 10) use the standard constants and sign but wrap the per-engine scores in sqrt((1/N) Σ S_i), which contradicts the plain sums in their Table 6. STAT (Chadha et al., 2022, Eq. 23, p. 74251) prints the early case without the minus sign in the exponent. Sun et al. (2025, Eq. 16, p. 216) use the standard constants and sign convention, but their equation is printed with the two cases split at d = 1 instead of d = 0. We use d = ŷ − y, with e^{−d/13} − 1 for d < 0 and e^{d/10} − 1 for d ≥ 0, summed over test engines. This follows the stated intent of Saxena et al. (2008) and the forms in Zhao et al. (2020, Eq. 12, p. 8) and Xu et al. (2023, Eq. 25, p. 11).

Never cited for the Score formula, its constants or its sign convention: DFormer (Liu et al., 2024a); STAR (Fan et al., 2024); Li et al. (2025, Sensors 25:3429); STAT (Chadha et al., 2022); Szrama (2026e, International Journal of Prognostics and Health Management 17(1); Eq. 8, p. 9, prints a 1/N mean instead of the sum; not in the footnote); Sun et al. (2025, ISA Transactions; Eq. 16 printed with the cases split at d = 1; printed page verified by Simon, RULES §34). Their Score values appear only in their own literature-table rows, labelled “their Eq. …” (STAT and Szrama (2026e) have no row, RULES §29, §33). Szrama 2026a and 2026b (R1.7 papers 3 and 1) print no Score formula and report no Score, so they are not on this list (RULES §40; research/round_05_r17_p1_p3_read.md §1.5, §2.4); Szrama 2026c (MSSP) prints no Score formula either (its Score values are its own, Table S17). Score sources: Saxena et al. (2008, IEEE PHM, pp. 1–9; primary, for the stated intent), with Zhao et al. (2020) and Xu et al. (2023) as the sources of the form. He et al. (2025) prints the standard form and is not in the footnote.

Per-subset claims allowed (D22 as amended, D51; secondary comparisons). All comparisons in this paragraph are secondary. The preregistered primary comparison, D4 against the validation-chosen best baseline pooled over 20 pairs, is inconclusive (exact Wilcoxon p 0.0696). A per-subset difference counts as significant (“reliably attributable”) if two conditions hold: the Holm-corrected p (over the 4 subsets of the comparison) is below 0.05, and the engine-bootstrap CI excludes 0 (D22). If the hierarchical (seeds × engines) CI of that cell includes 0, the cell is reported with that qualifier and is not called significant (D51). In v4, 9 cells meet both D22 conditions; 8 of them are claimable. Addendum C.3 and D51 say “10 cells”, but the cells they list add up to 9: θ* 2, iTransformer 1, PatchTST 1, LSTM 1, ridge 4. A recount from the per-subset table above also gives 9, and this has been flagged to eswa-reviewer:

  • Round-3 rows. The rule is met by D4 − θ* on FD002 (−2.22, Holm p 0.024, engine-bootstrap CI [−2.12, −0.30]) and on FD003 (−2.08, Holm p 0.021, CI [−2.26, −0.09]), and by D4 − iTransformer on FD002 (−1.62, Holm p 0.0013, CI [−2.28, −0.51]). For these three cells, the hierarchical bootstrap (R2.10) also gives CIs that exclude 0: [−3.58, −1.07], [−3.77, −0.45] and [−2.58, −0.72].
  • PatchTST FD002: listed, not claimed. D4 − PatchTST on FD002 (−0.61, Holm p 0.0004, CI [−1.43, −0.11]) meets both numerical conditions. Its hierarchical CI [−1.31, +0.03] includes 0, so we do not call this difference significant. Pooled over the four subsets, D4 − PatchTST is not significant either (exact Wilcoxon p 0.048 uncorrected, 0.145 after Holm over five pooled comparisons, a family that was not preregistered; D12).
  • Round-4 rows. D4 − LSTM: FD003 meets the rule (−3.68, Holm p 0.0011, CI [−5.57, −0.75]; hierarchical [−6.24, −1.37]). FD002 does not (engine CI [−2.20, +0.26]). On FD004 the LSTM had the lower test RMSE (D34). D4 − ridge meets the rule on FD001–FD004. For FD001, the hierarchical CI for D4 − ridge, [−4.44, −0.01], lies within Monte Carlo error of 0 (D48).
  • Never claimed. D4 against the best baseline Bk and D4 against Crossformer meet the rule on no subset. No FD001 or FD004 cell meets it except ridge. No sentence of the form “D4 significantly outperforms the baselines” is allowed. Every per-subset statement carries “secondary”, and the paragraph that contains it also states the primary result.

Source: workspace/experiments/final/posthoc_R1.24/regime_results.md (workspace, not in release) (b372533d…), single post-hoc descriptive read (log row 403); TR-fitted k-means regimes at the window's last cycle; RUL_FD004.txt never opened. Paired t CIs are descriptive and uncorrected across many metrics.

  • FD004 RMSE Δ (D4 − θ*) −0.60 [−1.40, +0.20]; Score −12.5 [−191, +166]: no difference shown.
  • D4 shifts Score from the early side (−90.1 [−171, −9.6]) to the late side (+77.6 [−102, +257], CI includes 0).
  • D4's Score is more concentrated: top-10 engines 55.5% vs 51.0% (Δ +4.4 points [+1.2, +7.6]); late-error > 20 engines carry 54.5% vs 45.4%; the number of such engines is the same (18.2 vs 18.2).
  • Regime R4 (op 25 / 0.62 / 60) carries the largest Score share (θ* 27.2%, D4 21.7%). No regime-level significance claim (R6 RMSE −1.10 [−2.21, +0.01] is borderline). No regime statement about the other baselines or the LSTM (not analysed). D4 does not have the best FD004 Score (LSTM 823).

8.11 k-means check for the operating conditions (R1.28; Supplementary Fig. S1)

On FD002 and FD004 the pipeline normalises sensors per operating condition with k-means (k = 6) on the three operating settings, fitted on the training engines of each split seed (section 5, step 2). k = 6 was fixed in the code before this check; the check confirms it after the fact and was not used to choose k (paper_plan D25; R1.28 PASS). The figure reads only the saved outputs of the post-hoc check (experiments/round_04_pre/exp_C2/outputs/k_selection_FD002.json, k_selection_FD004.json); no clustering was re-run. No silhouette or inertia value is typed here.

9. Validation and statistical rigor

  • Splits. Frozen engine-level splits data_splits.json (sha256 88840135…6eab). Split seeds 0–4: five fixed, pre-stated engine-level train/validation splits (repeated hold-out over training engines), not K-fold and not leave-one-engine-out (D23, D40). Tuning uses split seed 0.
  • Cost of 5-fold cross-validation (R1.10). Wording copied from the R1.10 answer in the response letter draft (workspace/docs/response_letter_draft_v01.md (workspace, not in release) §2.12, Cost bullet): 5-fold cross-validation would repeat the full tuning-and-retraining protocol 5 times per model: about 15 GPU-h for D4 (excluding the stage-1 design screen), 53 for θ* and 47 for the three external baselines together. These figures were measured without deterministic algorithms. With deterministic algorithms, the measured time per training step was 1.24–1.29 times higher for D4, 1.20–1.75 times for θ* and 1.04–1.26 times for the three external baselines; we did not measure this factor for the whole protocol [workspace/experiments/round_04_pre/exp_P0/results/table.md (workspace, not in release); workspace/concerns.md (workspace, not in release) R1.10; workspace/paper_plan.md (workspace, not in release) D23]. Leave-one-engine-out would cost more.
  • Leakage checks. All preprocessing fitted on TR engines of each split seed (SIZE refits on TRk(f) in both training and evaluation modules). test_guard in every tuning and training process. The released code removes every test-metric selection line (improve_transformer.py:1202/1314, MainSingleEng_FD001_F2_FD003_F4_Final.py:1245; RULES §20, §21).
  • Test discipline. workspace/experiments/test_eval_log.csv (workspace, not in release): 404 data rows (sha256 02a769a7…5a57). Rows 1–261: reads before round 4 (one per final configuration and seed). Rows 262–401: 140 round-4 reads (NOSMOOTH 20, SIZE 60, LN 20, LSTM 20, ridge 20; purposes r4_final_ablation / r4_final_baseline), one per manifest key, each after its frozen selection, none repeated, nothing selected from them. Rows 402–404: 3 analysis_posthoc rows (R2.10, R1.24, R0.23 + (c)) that re-read saved prediction files. Round 5 and the (b) simulation made 0 test reads. The v4 generator and the reviewer recompute re-read saved prediction files without evaluating any model; no new test read (D37, D41, D48). The main D4, θ* and baseline rows were read once.
  • Selection. D4 was chosen among 4 designs on validation; its total search is larger than any other row's (disclosed). Every model, including LSTM and ridge, got the same 12-trial rule (same trial rule, not same GPU-h; D7). Nothing in rounds 4–5 re-selected D4.
  • Determinism. Strict mode in every round-4/5 run: torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=False), CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8, memory fill on, cudnn deterministic, no benchmark, no TF32. CERT: 20/20 seed-0 cells bitwise. Reviewer re-runs bitwise: LN FD001 s0, LSTM FD001 s0, NOSMOOTH FD002 s0, WIN L30 FD002 s0 (bypass). Seeds 1–4 of the round-2/3 rows were not re-run in strict mode, so every round-4 paired comparison is mixed mode. Allowed: "all round-4 runs used strict deterministic mode; the 20 seed-0 cells of the five main models and the re-run round-4/5 trainings reproduced bit for bit on the same machine". Not allowed: "every reported number is bitwise reproducible"; cross-hardware claims (D36, D41).
  • Tests. Per subset: paired t 95% CI, Holm over 4 subsets; exact Wilcoxon (floor 0.0625 at n = 5). Pooled: exact Wilcoxon over 20 pairs. Effect size: gz with exact noncentral-t CI for dz. Engine level: paired percentile bootstrap and DM-HLN on seed-averaged predictions. Hierarchical seeds × engines bootstrap (conservative). SIZE: Page's L. Percentile seed bootstrap only as a labelled supplement (under-covers).
  • Multiplicity. The only confirmatory test is the round-3 preregistered primary. Holm-5 and Holm-7 pooled families are not preregistered. Round-4/5 arms are sensitivity analyses. Per-subset claims are secondary. Each needs Holm p < 0.05 over the 4 subsets of its comparison and an engine-bootstrap CI that excludes 0 (D22). A cell whose hierarchical CI includes 0 is not called significant (D51; this applies only to PatchTST FD002).
  • Recompute gates. R² identity holds to 1.1e-16; metrics from prediction files equal metrics.json (max diff 0); engines and labels identical across rows; 0 batch-invariance flags; v3 and exp_C4 reproduced byte-identically by the v4 generator.
  • Release reproduction checks. Check 1: six FD001 split-seed-0 validation retrains matched the frozen runs bit for bit (booleans only), with documented limits (history, section 13.3). Check 2, on the shipped code (authorised by Simon, RULES §25): the same six retrains matched again (booleans only), with the shipped-tree manifest equal before and after the run. Check 2 supersedes check 1's limits for the shipped code, for FD001 split seed 0 only (section 13.3).
  • Freeze gates. FZ1–FZ4 hold: no GPU training after the freeze (last GPU training artifact 2026-10-26 08:25), no reported number from a post-freeze run, log growth only by the three authorised rows, no gpu.lock (verdicts/round_05.md Addendum B.1).

TermMeaning
C-MAPSS, FD001–FD004NASA turbofan degradation simulation data and its four subsets
RULremaining useful life in cycles (labels capped at 125)
RMSE, MAE, R²root mean squared error, mean absolute error, coefficient of determination
NASA Scoreasymmetric per-engine error score, e^(−d/13) − 1 if d < 0, e^(d/10) − 1 if d ≥ 0, summed; d = prediction − truth
MHA, SDPAmulti-head attention; PyTorch scaled dot-product attention
ProbSparse, lazy rowInformer attention keeping only u queries; a non-kept row outputs mean(V)
TBNTransformer encoder layer with BatchNorm
BN, LNbatch normalisation, layer normalisation
EMAcausal exponential moving average, α = 0.24723
PE, FFNsinusoidal positional encoding; feed-forward network
LSTMlong short-term memory recurrent network
Ridgelinear regression with penalty α‖w‖²
SACA, D1–D4sensor-anchored cross-dimension attention (D4); round-3 designs EXACT, SENSOR-TOKEN, SENSOR-ALIGNED DUAL, SACA
θ*, θ0, Bkvalidation-tuned corrected original model; test-tuned checkpoint configuration (reference only); validation-chosen best baseline of subset k
ITTsubmitted improved training recipe (removed)
P2tuning protocol: 3 studies × 4 completed random-search trials (12 trials) per model and subset
TR, VA, TEtraining, validation and test engines
Common supportVA windows with label cycle ≥ 51
End paddingtest engine with T < L observed cycles: L − T copies of the last row appended
F0, F1, F2freeze points: manifest; LSTM/ridge selection; per-run selection file before the test read
CERT, strict modedeterminism certification; deterministic algorithms (warn_only False) + CUBLAS workspace setting
NInon-inferiority (margin 0.5 RMSE cycles)
gz, dzstandardised mean of paired differences (small-sample corrected), its population value
DM-HLNDiebold-Mariano test with the Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold correction
Holm; Page's Lstep-down multiple-test correction; rank test for a monotone trend
analysis_posthoclogged re-read of saved test predictions, descriptive, never used for selection
†, ‡, §bypass L = 30 cells; LSTM conservative-row note; ridge range/seed note
N, N′patch count without padding ⌊(L − P)/S⌋ + 1; with D4 end padding ⌊(L − P)/S⌋ + 2
FZ1–FZ4freeze gates: no GPU training after the freeze; no reported number from a post-freeze run; no test-log growth beyond the authorised rows; no gpu.lock left

13.3 Reproduction checks and their limits (README §5)

Two GPU reproduction checks ran, both validation only and both reporting booleans only. Check 2 ran on the shipped code and is the current evidence. Check 1 is kept below as the record of what happened (history).

Check 2: second GPU reproduction check, on the shipped code (current evidence)

  • Authorisation. Authorised by Simon on 2026-10-27 (RULES §25, an exception to freeze gate FZ1). The notice was logged in workspace/comms.md before the launch.
  • What ran. The same six cells as check 1 (FD001, split seed 0, validation only, strict deterministic mode): D4 (exp_B16), θ* (exp_B6), PatchTST (exp_B10_topup), iTransformer (exp_B11), Crossformer (exp_B12), LSTM (exp_V2). They were retrained from the shipped final/ tree through python -m saca_rul.cli train, one invocation per model, under workspace/gpu.lock. The repro sub-command was not used, because it writes all six cells into one folder with the same run tag, so each cell would overwrite the one before (RULES §25(b) forbids that). Each model has its own output folder. The comparison used the shipped runner.compare_with_frozen.
  • When. 2026-10-27, 11:02:58 to 11:10:28 local time. No test read (test log still 404 rows), no lock left behind.
  • Shipped-tree manifest. sha256 of every file under src/, configs/ (including configs/selections/) and scripts/: 111 files, tree sha256 639a92e5d32b5272f15b4280f1cc039fc6adc62e858a84e3c424b4d0026eb06b (workspace/review/repro_check_2/shipped_tree_manifest.json (workspace, not in release); after the run: workspace/review/repro_check_2/shipped_tree_after_run.json (workspace, not in release)). Recorded before the launch and re-hashed after the run: equal. Nothing under final/ was edited, linted or tested during the run (run-integrity rule, RULES §25).
  • Result (booleans only). final/results/repro_check/repro_result_2.json (sha256 3dcf8de3…): best epoch, state-dict sha256 and preds_val.csv sha256 equal to the frozen run for all six models (6 of 6); all_match true; shipped_tree_equal_before_and_after true.
  • Run folder. Kept whole and never deleted: workspace/experiments/final/repro_check_2/ (workspace/experiments/final/repro_check_2/; workspace, not in release) (outside final/). Its files hold numbers and are marked "not reported" in its README.md.
  • Status of check 1. Because all six cells match on the shipped code, the limits of check 1 (code edited during the run, deleted run folders) are superseded by check 2 for the shipped code, for FD001 split seed 0 only. The check-1 text below stays as the record.

Scope of both checks

  • Seed 0 only. Each check covers one subset and one split seed (FD001, seed 0) for six models. Neither says anything about FD002–FD004 or seeds 1–4 (seeds 1–4 of the round-2/3 rows were never re-run in strict mode, D36), nor about other hardware.

Check 1 (history; superseded by check 2 for the shipped code)

Kept as written in final v01, apart from this label. It records the edits made during the run, the deleted run folders and the overwrite incident.

  • What ran (check 1). Pre-logged in comms.md: six validation-only retrains in strict deterministic mode, all FD001, split seed 0: D4 (exp_B16), θ* (exp_B6), PatchTST (exp_B10_topup), iTransformer (exp_B11), Crossformer (exp_B12), LSTM (exp_V2). Pass criterion as R4-CERT: best epoch, state-dict sha256 and preds_val.csv sha256 equal to the frozen run. Result (final/results/repro_check/repro_result.json, sha256 f5b455a0…, booleans only): 6 of 6 match. No test read, no log row, no lock left.
  • Limit 1: code edited during the run. The relaunch ran 04:37:53–04:44:59 while the shipped code was being edited (ruff --fix over the tree at 04:39:29, typing and lint edits, new tune/freeze sub-commands in cli.py, a verify.py edit). The match therefore certifies the 04:37:53 tree, not the shipped tree.
  • Limit 2: deleted evidence. At 04:37:36 the folder of the aborted first launch was removed; at 04:45 the relaunch run folders (ckpt_rmse.pt, preds_val.csv, train.log) and repro_stdout.log were removed, against RULES §2. The 6/6 match cannot be re-checked from run artifacts; only the booleans and the transcript lines remain.
  • Option A evidence (CPU, no data, no number). The 04:37:53 tree was reconstructed by replaying the build session's Write and Bash calls (final/results/repro_check/launch_tree/, reconstruction/); replaying the post-launch steps on top of it gave the shipped .py files byte for byte (replay_check.md, check of 05:07). Six files changed after that check (cli.py, shapes.py, figures.py, posthoc_r124.py, tests/test_frozen.py, scripts/make_release_list.py; named in replay_check.md and README §5). scripts/ast_equivalence.py (results/repro_check/ast_equivalence.md, sha256 42154c5c…, re-run byte-identically by the reviewer): 37 modules, 29 equal, 5 differ with every hunk listed and explained; on the reproduction path 17 of 17 are equal or explained (residuals in attention.py, data.py, cli.py). Its “shipped sha” column is now stale for two files off the reproduction path, figures.py (changed by the RULES §37 recolour) and tests/test_data_eval_pipeline.py; a fresh run still reports 17 of 17 reproduction-path modules equal or explained. It is a dated record and was not regenerated (review/final_check_14.md advisory A2). The vendored tree is byte-identical to the launch tree. Final-check 02 accepted option A for README §5 as worded.
  • Limit 3: what option A is not. The reconstruction comes from the transcript, not a saved copy; "AST-equal" is not proof of equal GPU behaviour; the three residuals are argued by reading, not by test.
  • Overwrite incident. During fix attempt 1 the replay tooling overwrote five files by mistake (figures.py, posthoc_r023.py, posthoc_r124.py, posthoc_r210.py, posthoc_valsim.py; the last with identical bytes). The replay rebuilt them, and their sha256 equalled the first release until figures.py was rewritten on purpose and posthoc_r124.py received a docstring change.
